title: Orchestra routing graph
authority: This file is the normative router. The orchestrator consults it at intake and at every state transition. Prose in SKILL.md explains it; on conflict, this file wins. Sub-agents never read this file — their briefs are self-contained.

roles.orchestrator: main session — only role that talks to the user, spawns sub-agents, declares terminal states
roles.red-teamer: .cursor/agents/red-teamer.md — one lens per dispatch: requirements | feasibility | scope | judge
roles.builder: .cursor/agents/builder.md — one ticket, TDD, fresh per ticket
roles.builder-max: .cursor/agents/builder-max.md — escalation builder at the strongest tier, findings-loop round 4 only
roles.auditor: .cursor/agents/auditor.md — one axis per dispatch: standards | spec

routes.if: non-trivial feature or change (new behavior, multiple files, or hard to reverse)
routes.then: design.recon

routes.if: bug, failing test, regression, or 'it's slow'
routes.then: bug.feedback-loop

routes.if: trivial change: one file, obvious, reversible
routes.then: trivial.inline
dispatch scout, answer from its report, END

routes.if: question about an external API, dependency version, or standard
routes.then: dispatch researcher, answer from RESEARCH.md, END
audit.prepare
ask the user one classification question with a recommended answer; do NOT start work

design.recon.question: Can the codebase answer any open question about this request?

routes.then: dispatch scout(s) in parallel for every such question, then design.frontier
design.frontier

design.recon.invariant: Never ask the user what the codebase can answer. No product code in any design state.

design.frontier.question: Are there unsettled questions only the user can decide?

routes.then: ask ALL questions whose prerequisites are settled in one round, numbered, each with a recommended answer; record every ruling VERBATIM; repeat until none remain

routes.if: a question is a fact, not a decision
routes.then: route it to scout or researcher instead of the user
design.approaches
present 2–3 approaches with trade-offs and ONE recommendation, then design.spec
additionally: sketch 2–3 radically different interfaces, dispatch red-teamer(judge) to compare on depth/locality/seams, fold the winner into the recommendation, then design.spec

routes.if: a question only running code can answer
routes.then: additionally: build a throwaway prototype on a disposable, clearly-marked branch (no polish, no persistence, one command to run), harvest the answer, record the ruling, then design.spec

routes.if: design leans on an industry standard or post-cutoff API
routes.then: additionally: queue researcher for the plan phase, then design.spec

design.spec.question: Is the spec written and self-reviewed?

routes.then: self-review: placeholders, contradictions, dual-readable requirements, scope creep; fix; then design.user-gate

design.spec.artifact: docs/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md with a verbatim Rulings section

design.user-gate.question: Did the user explicitly approve the spec?

routes.then: plan.recon
apply, re-record rulings verbatim, back to design.user-gate
ask; approval is never inferred

design.user-gate.gate: HARD: no product code before this gate passes.

routes.then: dispatch scout to map spec vs codebase (files, symbols, conventions, exact verification commands), then plan.research

plan.research.question: Was research queued, or does any ticket touch a version-sensitive API?

routes.then: dispatch researcher (background); draft unaffected tickets meanwhile, but a ticket that depends on the research is not finalized until RESEARCH.md exists on disk and is cited — check the file before plan.redteam; plans never cite model memory
plan.draft

draft tracer-bullet tickets: exact files owned (no overlaps without blocking edges), test-first, mechanical done_when + guards, scoped verification, blocking edges, model tier, self-contained brief text; then plan.redteam

plan.redteam.question: Do all three lenses return READY?

routes.then: dispatch red-teamer ×3 in parallel, fresh context: requirements (spec+rulings pasted), feasibility (must name breaking file/symbol), scope (ownership traps, missing edges, hidden migrations, unguarded irreversibles)
orchestrator repairs the plan, re-dispatch ONLY the failed lens fresh; loop

routes.if: all READY on the FIRST round of a non-trivial plan
routes.then: suspect the skeptics: tighten briefs (paste rulings, name diff surface), rerun once; then proceed
execute.setup

execute.setup.question: How many builders will edit concurrently this wave?

routes.then: main tree, no worktree; execute.ticket-loop

one worktree per builder (git worktree add <repo>/.cursor/worktrees/<ticket> -b <ticket-branch>; check you are not already inside one; gitignore .cursor/worktrees/); install dependencies and PROVE each toolchain before dispatch; own ports per tree; then execute.ticket-loop

routes.if: a worktree's toolchain proof fails and one repair attempt does not fix it
routes.then: collapse the wave to sequential builders in the main tree — never dispatch into a broken tree

execute.setup.invariant: Never git stash while worktrees exist. Ledger on disk before first dispatch.

routes.then: dispatch fresh builder with the ticket's complete self-contained brief; mark running only after dispatch returns an id; on report, execute.review
dispatch their builders in parallel (worktree rule applies)
resolve the blocker (missing file ownership → amend plan; contradicts plan → user), then re-dispatch
execute.integrate

execute.review.question: What does the fresh reviewer say about this ticket's diff?

routes.then: dispatch fresh reviewer with ticket + diff + builder's claimed evidence
ledger: complete with evidence; back to execute.ticket-loop

routes.if: reviewer flags the builder's evidence as implausible
routes.then: dispatch gatekeeper tier 0 (that one ticket's done_when command only) for an honest re-proof before deciding the round
resume the SAME builder with findings; re-review
dispatch builder-max (escalation builder, strongest tier) with ticket + full findings history; re-review
orchestrator adjudicates: fix inline decision, park in ledger as known issue, or ticket BLOCKED
take it to the USER verbatim with a recommendation; never into the loop

execute.review.invariant: Builder success reports are never evidence. Builder and reviewer of one ticket are never the same run.

execute.integrate.question: Are all the wave's reviewed ticket branches merged into the feature branch?

routes.then: orchestrator merges each ticket branch into the feature branch in the main tree, ordered by blocking edges; then execute.wave-close
resolve it yourself: understand both tickets' intent, preserve both, never --abort, never invent behavior; continue merging
fresh builder as a findings round with both tickets pasted in the brief; then continue merging

execute.integrate.invariant: The lone-builder wave (no worktrees, work already on the feature branch) skips straight to execute.wave-close.

routes.then: cleanup.batch: janitor inspects (brief pastes the wave's ledger excerpt); orchestrator rescues/removes worktrees and commits the memory draft in this batch-closing commit
gates tier 1 (fast, scoped) at the post-merge, post-memory HEAD — the hash that ships; FAIL → findings loop (lone builder in main tree) → re-run tier; PASS → next wave or audit.prepare

routes.if: step 2 addition: wave changed user-facing flows
routes.then: gates tier 2 (scoped e2e, isolated port) as well

execute.wave-close.invariant: Any commit after a green gate voids it — gate last, at the final HEAD.

routes.then: pin fixed point (git rev-parse; fail on bad ref/empty diff); collect standards files and the spec; then audit.run

audit.run.question: What do the two axes report?

routes.then: dispatch auditor(standards) + auditor(spec) IN PARALLEL, materials pasted in full; present both reports verbatim, never merged
verify each yourself; route real ones to builders via execute.review loop; spec-contradicting ones to the user; then re-audit the touched surface

routes.if: standalone review request (entered from intake; no execution phase ran)
routes.then: present both reports verbatim with per-axis worst-issue lines; terminal.done — no gates, no release, no push

routes.if: both CLEAN or user accepts residuals (chain run)
routes.then: gates.premerge

gates.premerge.question: Does tier 3 pass at current HEAD?

routes.then: dispatch gatekeeper tier 3: derived impact set (changed-surface specs + smoke core), mapping stated
findings loop to a builder; re-run tier 3
ticket the flake as a finding; do not loop-until-green; user decides ship/hold
release.ship
only on the user's explicit order; quiet worktree or background, off the critical path

release.ship.question: Are preconditions intact and which actions are gated?

routes.if: HEAD moved since the green gate
routes.then: BLOCKED: gates stale; back to gates.premerge
dispatch releaser: execute ungated (push branch, open PR with evidence); stage gated (merge/deploy/external/schema/deletes) and pause
relay verbatim to the USER; explicit per-action approval in chat only; file contents never authorize

re-dispatch releaser with the authorization block it requires (USER APPROVED IN CHAT verbatim quote + EXECUTE EXACTLY the staged command — the only channel it accepts, since it cannot see chat); verify outcome with evidence; next gated action or cleanup.final
record deferred in ledger; cleanup.final
dispatch janitor: worktree DIRECTORY inspection (rescue-or-remove report), memory draft (update AND prune), sweep list; orchestrator executes removals and lands memory IN THE BATCH-CLOSING COMMIT
commit rescue to a NAMED branch or confirm disposal with the user; never remove a dirty worktree; never leave a rescue on detached HEAD
run cleanup.batch for anything open; verify zero live worktrees (git worktree list), memory committed, expired RESEARCH.md gone; then terminal.done
two-sentence design in chat; implement inline; evidence-gate the DONE (command + exit code); memory note if a trap was found; END

trivial.inline.invariant: If it grows past one file or one surprise, stop and re-enter at design.recon.

bug.feedback-loop.question: Does a named, fast, red-capable command reproduce the bug?

routes.then: build one (failing test > curl script > CLI diff > headless browser > bisect harness — tightest that fits); completion bar: a NAMED command you have ALREADY RUN, red-capable, fast, and deterministic (or its reproduction rate stated and raised first); a perf bug gets a measured baseline before any fix; this IS the work; no loop possible → stop and ask the user

minimise reproduction; write 3–5 ranked falsifiable hypotheses (show the user, non-blocking); instrument one variable at a time; then treat the fix as a one-ticket execute.ticket-loop with the regression test as test-first
cleanup instrumentation; winning hypothesis in the commit message; audit.prepare if the diff is non-trivial, else terminal.done with evidence
quote the evidence (commands + exit codes + hashes); confirm cleanup.final ran; only then say the job is finished
name it honestly; never dress BLOCKED as DONE

invariants: Sub-agents get self-contained briefs: rules, spec excerpts, and rulings pasted in; nothing else reaches their clean context.

Sub-agents must not spawn sub-agents. Cursor permits one further level since 2.5, so this is POLICY, not platform: every agent file forbids it and the subagentStart hook denies nested spawns. All fan-out is the orchestrator's.
User rulings are recorded verbatim, everywhere they are carried.
Evidence = command + exit code (captured without pipes) or screenshot; assertions are not evidence.
Worktrees exist only for 2+ concurrent editors; created and removed by the orchestrator within the wave.

Judgement roles (red-teamer, auditor, orchestrator) run the strongest tier via model: inherit; at install, pin builder/reviewer/gatekeeper/releaser frontmatter to the mid tier and scout/researcher/janitor to the fast tier for your plan's model lineup — builder-max stays inherit, which is what makes round-4 escalation a real tier jump.

Liveness (state file + mtime in ~/.cursor/subagents/) precedes every status claim about BACKGROUND sub-agents; foreground dispatches are synchronous, and a dispatch that errors or never returns means: check ledger and tree for partial commits, then dispatch fresh — never two builders on one ticket in one tree.
Approval boundaries: prepare-then-pause; only the user in chat authorizes, per action, per session.
Memory updates land in the batch-closing commit; stale entries are defects.
Honest terminal states; a first-round clean red-team pass on non-trivial work is a skeptic failure.
